warmup.text: Nita has died, and her family carries her on the walk. In Chapter 12, Isaac learns that Nita's family has a secret. Before you read, think about secrets. When is it right to keep one, and when is it right to tell? Your reading lens this week is how a story's pressure builds.

words.text: Two new roots this week, and both are about feeling. One leans toward emotion. One leans toward the senses. Then listen to long words. When a word grows, its strongest beat can move. In the council fire game, say each word out loud and tap the beat you say the strongest.

reading.text: Read Chapter 12 of How I Became a Ghost in your book. Nita's ghost comes to Isaac with a request: find her sister. Watch what happens when Isaac asks Gabe about it, and notice what makes the tension grow. Then do the Virtue Watch and the Read Like a Writer box.

assignment.text: Three questions about Chapter 12, then the plan for a theme paragraph. A theme is a big idea the book shows, like courage or justice. Today you only pick one and note two pieces of evidence. Copy your work into Canvas when you finish.

hook.q: Someone you trust says, “Do not tell anyone.” When is it right to keep a secret, and when is it right to tell?

game.title: Council Fire
game.sub: This week's word game · 5 logs today
game.look: On the walk, families gather around a fire every night. In this game, each pair of related words is a log. Say each word and tap the beat you say the strongest. Get both words right and the log goes on the fire. Your fire keeps burning all week.

art.title: Snowstorm in the Sierras
art.alt: A painting of a stagecoach pulled by horses through a thick snowstorm, with bare trees and a pale sun.
art.look: William Hahn painted this snowstorm in the Sierra Nevada mountains of California in 1876. It is far from Isaac's road, but it shows the kind of storm in Chapter 12: snow swirling so thick that the walkers are blinded by it.

art.creator: William Hahn

virtue.name: justice
virtue.title: Justice or not?
virtue.intro: You just read Chapter 12. Read each moment. Tap Justice or Not justice.

items.t: Isaac follows Gabe into the woods and says, “I want to help you find your other daughter.”
items.why: He sees that something is wrong and offers to help set it right. That is the start of justice.

items.t: Gabe says, “We do not have another daughter. Do not speak of this!”
items.why: Gabe is frightened, and his fear makes sense. But keeping a wrong hidden is not justice yet.

items.t: To make Gabe listen, Isaac shares his own secret: he will soon be a ghost.
items.why: He trusts Gabe with the truth so the truth about Nita's sister can come out. Telling the truth is part of justice.

items.t: Walking blind in the snow, Isaac imagines an icicle falling on him.
items.why: That is a frightening daydream, not a choice about right and wrong.
